candidates.change_summary: Change the returned selector to a different constant (return 0x150b7a02 instead of the standard ERC721TokenReceiver selector) so the function completes but returns a different bytes4 value.
Return zero (0x00000000) instead of the ERC721TokenReceiver selector; call still completes but returns a different bytes4 value.
Return the bitwise-negation of the ERC721TokenReceiver selector, producing a different bytes4 value while still completing.
Return the selector of a different well-known hook (IERC3156FlashBorrower.onFlashLoan) to change the returned bytes4 value while still completing.
Set baseToken to address(0) unconditionally instead of assigning the provided _baseToken argument.
Assign baseToken to msg.sender instead of the provided _baseToken argument.
Swap assignment: assign nft from _baseToken and baseToken from _nft, effectively swapping the two provided addresses.
Assign _nft to nft after other initializations instead of near the top (moves the nft assignment statement later), changing nft value if other code uses nft-dependent behavior during initialization.
Do not set nft at all during initialization (delete the nft assignment), leaving nft at its prior value.
Assign nft to the zero address instead of _nft to intentionally change stored nft value.
Replace the assignment to changeFee so initialize sets changeFee to _changeFee + 1 (increments input), changing stored value.
Replace the assignment to changeFee so initialize sets changeFee to _changeFee - 1 (decrements input), changing stored value.
Replace the assignment to changeFee so initialize sets changeFee to a constant 0, altering stored value.
Delete the assignment to changeFee so initialize leaves changeFee at its default (zero) unless previously set, changing stored value.
Remove the validation that prevents a feeRate > 5000 by changing the require revert check to allow any feeRate (deleted the FeeRateTooHigh check).
Clamp the supplied _feeRate to zero before assignment (force feeRate = 0 regardless of input).

Swap assignment order to set feeRate before validating fee cap, causing the state to momentarily accept the value before revert (but still revert if too high) — here we move the feeRate assignment earlier so behavior upon successful init differs in ordering (observable feeRate remains same but changed statement order).
Change the check that prevents re-initialization from reverting to instead being a no-op (commented out), so initialize can run multiple times and set initialized = true even if it was already true.

Invert the initial check so initialize reverts if NOT already initialized, preventing the first-time initialization and leaving initialized false after a successful call (changes observable initialized).
Move the assignment 'initialized = true' to the start of the function so initialized becomes true before checks and state assignments, altering observable value if initialize reverts later.
